content.title: How to watch Arkansas vs High Point channel stream game time
content.text: Here's everything you need to know to tune in to Arkansas' Round of 32 matchup vs. High Point in the Moda Center.The No. 4-seeded Arkansas Razorbacks (27-8, 13-5, SEC) look to advance to the Sweet 16 against the No. 12-seeded High Point Panthers (31-4, 15-1, Big South) on Saturday night. Tip-off from the Moda Center in Portland (Ore.) is at 8:45 p.m. (CDT), and the game will be televised by TBS.Saturday's matchup will be the second between the two programs. The last time Arkansas and High Point faced off was in 2013, and the Hogs dominated the Panthers in Bud Walton Arena, 89-48. If Arkansas wins on Saturday, it'll take on the winner of 1-seeded Arizona vs. 9-seeded Utah State in the Sweet 16.Tip-off between the Hogs and Panthers is set for 8:45 p.m. (CDT), and the game will be televised by TBS.WHO: No. 4-seeded Arkansas Razorbacks (27-8, 13-5, SEC) vs. No. 12-seeded High Point Panthers (31-4, 15-1, Big South)WHEN: Saturday, Mar. 21, at 8:45 p.m. (CDT)WHERE: Moda Center (19,393) | Portland, Ore.TV/STREAM: TBSBET SARACEN ODDS: Arkansas -11.5 | Over/Under: 168.5RADIO STATIONS: Sirius Ch. 99, XM Ch. 190 | Batesville KWOZ-FM 103.3 | Batesville KBTA-AM 1340 | Camden KCXY-FM 95.3 | Camden KAMD-FM 97.1 | Crossett KAGH-AM 800 | Crossett KAGH-FM 104.9 | De Queen KDQN-FM 92.1 | DeWitt KDEW-FM 97.3 | El Dorado KMRX-FM 96.1 | Fayetteville KAKS-FM 99.5 | Fayetteville KUOA-AM 1290 | Fayetteville KQSM-FM 92.1 | Fayetteville KUOA-FM 95.3 | Fayetteville KBVA-FM HD3 106.5 | Forrest City KBFC-FM 93.5 | Fort Smith KERX-FM 95.3 | Glenwood KHGZ-AM 670 | Glenwood KHGZ-FM 98.9 | Hot Springs/Mena KTTG-FM 96.3 | Jonesboro KEGI-FM 100.5 | Little Rock KABZ-FM 103.7 | Magnolia KZHE-FM 100.5 | Marshall KBCN-FM 104.3 | 96.3 Monett (Mo.) KWXM-FM 102.3 | Searcy KSMD-FM 99.1 | Texarkana (Tex.) KKTK-AM 1400 | Wynne KWYN-FM 92.5 | TuneInHIGH POINT PANTHERS SNAPSHOTThe Panthers are in their first season under head coach Flynn Clayman. Things went pretty well for Clayman in his first season with the Panthers, as he led the team to a 31-4 record, including a 15-1 record in Big South play. To advance to the Round of 32, High Point defeated 5-seeded Wisconsin on Thursday in the Round of 64, 83-82.High Point has three players averaging double-digit scoring this season, but senior forward Terry Anderson is leading the way with 16 points per game.ARKANSAS RAZORBACKS SNAPSHOTThe Hogs are in their second season under head coach John Calipari, and they're 49-22 during his time in Fayetteville and 21-14 in SEC play. Calipari and the Razorbacks advanced to the Round of 32 after defeating Hawaii in the Round of 64 on Thursday, 97-78. Arkansas has four players averaging double-digit scoring, but freshman point guard Darius Acuff Jr. is leading the way for the Razorbacks with 23 points per game, and he also averages a team-high 6.6 assists per game. Thanks for listening!Arkansas blasts South Carolina, 22-6 (7)The fourth-ranked Razorbacks took it to South Carolina early and often in a 22-6 beatdown in seven innings.Arkansas plated 17 runs in the first four innings and kept pouring it on as the No. 4 Razorbacks took a 22-6 series-opening win over struggling South Carolina Friday night at Founders Park in Columbia (S.C.). Here's a breakdown of how the Hogs moved to 3-1 in conference play with a dominant performance against the Gamecocks. HOW ARKANSAS WONSouth Carolina came into this game with plenty of questions and concerns while riding a five-game losing streak, but their uninspired play and pair of errors had very little to do with this lopsided result. Arkansas started red-hot with 4 runs in the first, 3 in the second, 2 more in the third, then broke it open with 8 runs in the fourth inning before the Gamecocks found the scoreboard.By the end of the fourth, Arkansas had 17 runs on 10 hits and Gabe Gaeckle had reached six strikeouts before allowing a couple of harmless 2-run homers. TJ Pompey made it five straight innings with runs in the fifth when he clobbered Bryce Navarre's offering and pushed the lead back to 19-4.Arkansas tacked on three more runs in the fifth and sixth frames, with its only downer of the day being three 2-run home runs allowed. Two were Gaeckle's and another was given up late by Luke Cornelison in a just-end-it seventh. TURNING POINTIt's not often that a Friday night game on the road feels over after just one inning, but that was the feeling in this one when Arkansas jumped out to a 4-0 lead and the Gamecocks stranded a pair of runners in the bottom half. The Hogs put up 3 more in the second and Gaeckle followed with a very quick 1-2-3 inning that sent the home team spiraling. (Photo: 247Sports)STANDOUT PERFORMERIt's a shame that Damian Ruiz (3 for 4, 3 RBI, 1 HR, 2 BB, 1 K, 1 E), Camden Kozeal (3 for 4, 3 RBI, 1 HR, 1 BB, 1 HBP) and TJ Pompey (2 for 4, 2 RBI, 1 HR) will be overshadowed in this one, but Maika Niu was just on his own level Friday night. He had a SportsCenterTop10-type catch in left center and went 3 for 5 at the plate with 6 RBI, a double, a walk, a pair of homers and a stolen base.MAIKA NIU ARE YOU SERIOUS 🤯 pic.twitter.com/Ugc4t27kDf— Arkansas Baseball (@RazorbackBSB) March 20, 2026BY THE NUMBERSArkansas scored 22 runs on 14 hits with 1 error and 9 men left on base. South Carolina was held to 6 runs on 9 hits and did all of its damage on 2-run homers. The Razorbacks' Gaeckle got the win to move to 3-1 with a 2.97 ERA. Josh Gunther took the loss for Carolina, dropping to 2-1.WHAT WE LEARNEDWhen Ryder Helfrick goes 0-3, Kuhio Aloy goes 1-5, Zack Stewart goes 0-3 and the Razorbacks still win a SEC Friday night game on the road 22-6, it says a lot about how well some of the new guys are coming along. It's only one game against a team that sometimes looks as awful as any SEC team we can remember in recent memory, but it's still a massive way to start a road series. In this one, we learned that Arkansas' huge lead was enough to let Gaeckle keep going for 5 full innings and 89 pitches before moving on to Jordan Martin and eventually Cornelison for the seventh and final frame. That means there's even more options for Saturday's 3 p.m. contest, which can be seen on SEC Network+.Arkansas faces challenge defending plethora of High Point 3-point threatsArkansas basketball will face a High Point team with multiple guys capable of going off from beyond the arc on any given night, led by veteran sharpshooter Chase Johnston. No. 4 seed Arkansas basketball didn't have to sweat its first round game in the NCAA Tournament on Thursday. The Razorbacks handled their business with ease and cruised to a 97-78 win over No. 13 seed Hawaii. Arkansas will now move on to face No. 12 seed High Point on Saturday, after the Panthers upset No. 5 seed Wisconsin, 83-82. Arkansas did a decent job limiting Hawaii from beyond the arc at times, but the Rainbow Warriors did get 30 points from three on some decent looks. That will be a key again on Saturday as High Point is a team that is not afraid to hoist threes and has some very capable threats. On the season, Arkansas' opponents are shooting just 31.8% from three, which ranks 56th in the country. The Panthers boast a 34.5% clip from beyond the arc, which ranks just 146th in the country. Their 3-point rate is 43.3%, which ranks 104th, meaning they're not afraid to make it a perimeter shooting contest.
